results.name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Row
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, and palms facing forward.
Pull the dumbbells towards your ribcage by squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your elbows pointed backward.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum to lift the weights; use controlled motions for effective muscle engagement.
Breathe out as you lift the dumbbells and breathe in as you lower them.
Ensure your body remains stable on the bench and avoid lifting your chest.
results.description: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, and palms facing each other.
Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until your arms are parallel to the floor, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your neck in a neutral position and avoid straining it during the exercise.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together to maximize the activation of your rear deltoids and upper back muscles.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to reduce joint strain.
results.description: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your arm extended down by your side, palm facing your thigh.
Keeping your arm straight, lift the dumbbell directly in front of you to shoulder height, ensuring your palm is facing downwards.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid swinging the dumbbell to use momentum.
Engage your core to maintain stability and control throughout the exercise.
Move the dumbbell in a slow and controlled manner to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand by your side with your palm facing your body. Keep your other hand on your hip or relaxed by your side.
Lift the dumbbell out to the side, maintaining a slight bend in your elbow. Raise your arm until it is parallel to the floor.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, keeping the movement smooth and controlled.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and deliberately for maximum control.
Avoid using momentum or swinging the dumbbell.
Keep your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Low Fly
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand. Extend your arm straight down in front of your body, palm facing forward.
Lift the dumbbell in front of you sideways in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise your arm until the dumbbell is at your eye level, keeping your shoulder muscle engaged.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the movement.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid using momentum.
Focus on using your chest and shoulder muscles to lift the weight.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Low Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Shoulder Press (Version 2)
instructions: Begin standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand at shoulder height with your palm facing forward. Place your left hand on your hip for stability.
Engage your core and press the dumbbell overhead by extending your right arm fully overhead.
Lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height with control, maintaining a steady and smooth motion.
Repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the dumbbell overhead and inhale as you lower it.
Avoid arching your back; maintain a neutral spine throughout the exercise.
Keep your movements controlled to prevent injury and ensure proper muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Shoulder Press (Version 2) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Plank Pullthrough
instructions: Begin in a high plank with your hands directly below your shoulders, your feet slightly apart, and a dumbbell positioned on the floor beside one hand.
Shift your weight onto one hand and reach your opposite hand underneath your torso to grasp the dumbbell.
Drag the dumbbell across the floor to the opposite side while keeping your shoulders and hips facing the floor.
Place your hand back on the floor, repeat the pull with the opposite arm, and continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your torso as you reach underneath.
Transfer your weight smoothly without collapsing into your supporting shoulder.
Drag the dumbbell across the floor instead of lifting it upward.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell across and inhale as you return your hand to the floor.
results.description: Dumbbell Plank Pullthrough is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Chest, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Push Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing each other. Keep your elbows close to your body.
Slightly bend your knees and lower your body into a quarter squat, then explosively extend your legs and perform a light jump to drive the dumbbells upward.
Press the dumbbells overhead by extending your arms fully, locking out your elbows at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height in a controlled manner and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use the power generated from your legs and the light jump to help drive the dumbbells overhead.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees to absorb the impact of the weights.
results.description: Dumbbell Push Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Glutes.

results.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
instructions: Kneel with your right knee on a bench and your left foot firmly planted on the floor for stability. Lean forward until your torso is parallel to the floor, and place your right hand on the bench for support. Hold a dumbbell in your left hand with an overhand grip, allowing it to hang straight down from your shoulder.
Row the dumbbell up towards your side, allowing your elbow to flare out to the side. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Hold the top position briefly, ensuring your upper arm is parallel to the floor and your elbow is pointing outward.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, allowing your arm to fully extend.
tips: Keep your elbow flared out to the side to target the rear delts effectively.
Exhale as you row the dumbbell up and inhale as you lower it back down.
Use a controlled and steady pace to maintain proper form and muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Rear Full Shrugs
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Hold the dumbbells behind your back at shoulder width, with your palms facing each other.
Lift your shoulders as high as possible towards your ears, squeezing your shoulders at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position with control, allowing your arms to fully extend.
tips: Avoid using momentum or jerking motions; focus on a slow and controlled movement.
Exhale as you lift your shoulders and inhale as you lower them back down.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid tensing it during the exercise.
results.description: Dumbbell Rear Full Shrugs is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.
